title: skillgrade
description: Unit tests for agent skills — run assertions against agent skill outputs the same way you'd test code
why_interesting: Solves the 'how do I know my agent skill actually works' problem with a familiar test-runner interface. From Minko Gechev (Angular team). 480 stars in ~3 months.

title: agent-skills-eval
description: Test runner for agentskills.io-style skills with YAML-based scenarios and LLM judges
why_interesting: 508 stars in 2 weeks. The agentskills.io spec is getting traction and this gives it a proper eval framework. TypeScript, works with OpenAI-compatible APIs.

title: eval-view
description: Regression testing for AI agents — snapshot behavior, diff tool calls, catch regressions in CI
why_interesting: Works with LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI, Anthropic. The snapshot-diff approach is exactly what agent teams need but few build. Python/pytest-based.

title: agent-belt
description: Reproducible evaluation for AI coding agents — multi-turn scenarios, rich assertions, multi-judge consensus
why_interesting: From JFrog's engineering team. Runs eval scenarios against Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, or any agent you plug in. Open source, CLI-based. Fills the 'how do I test my coding agent doesn't break' gap.

title: contrabass
description: Project-level orchestrator for AI coding agents — Go + Charm TUI implementation of OpenAI's Symphony SPEC.md
why_interesting: First real implementation of the Symphony spec. Go binary, TUI interface, coordinates Codex/Claude Code agents. 151 stars, actively maintained. The 'one orchestrator, many coding CLIs' pattern is where agent infra is heading.

title: TraceFix
description: Uses TLA+ counterexamples to repair multi-agent LLM coordination protocols before deployment
why_interesting: Formal methods applied to agent coordination. Instead of testing protocols after they fail, TLA+ finds violations upfront and generates repairs. CAISconf 2026 paper by Rutgers team.

title: Raindrop Workshop
description: Local debugger for AI agents — live streamed traces of every token, tool call, and decision with self-healing eval loops
why_interesting: Solves the 'agent debugging is blind' problem. You can watch agents think in real time, and Claude Code reads the traces, writes evals, and fixes bugs autonomously. MIT license, 665 stars in 18 days. Works with every major SDK and coding agent.

title: claude-mem
description: Persistent context across sessions for coding agents — captures session activity, compresses with AI, injects into future sessions
why_interesting: Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot. 76k stars, v13.2, active commits. Solves the real problem of agents starting from zero every session. SQLite + ChromaDB + embeddings under the hood.

title: 12-Factor Agents
description: Engineering principles for building production-grade LLM-powered software — agents as software with LLM steps, not prompt loops
why_interesting: 21k stars. The core insight: agents are software with LLM calls placed strategically, not 'prompt + tools + loop'. Own your prompts, typed tools, human-in-the-loop as first-class, stateless reducer pattern. This is the production playbook most agent projects lack.

title: Context7
description: Up-to-date code documentation delivered to LLMs and code editors via MCP — solves the stale-doc problem for coding agents
why_interesting: 55k stars, MIT. The real issue: every coding agent guesses APIs from training data that's months old. Context7 injects fresh docs at query time. Works as MCP server, integrates with Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex. Built by Upstash. The 'documentation as context' pattern is a missing infra layer for agent reliability.

title: Chrome DevTools MCP
description: Official Chrome DevTools exposed as MCP server — lets coding agents inspect, debug, and profile web apps directly
why_interesting: 40k stars, Apache 2.0, official Google project. The first serious bridge between browser debugging and agent workflows. Agents can now read console errors, inspect DOM, profile performance, and set breakpoints — all through structured tool calls instead of screenshot guessing. Changes how agents debug frontend code.

title: Lapdog (Datadog)
description: Local agent tracer — traces reasoning and tool calls from Codex, Claude Code, and Pi in real time, no account required
why_interesting: Datadog shipped a free local tool that shows what agents actually do. 70 likes in hours. Fills a real gap: most agent debugging is reading terminal output blind. Runs fully local, zero infra. The 'observability for agents' layer is barely starting and this is the first usable tool from a major vendor.

title: Retrieval Routing: vector + GraphRAG + PageIndex
description: Production pattern: route queries across vector RAG, GraphRAG, and PageIndex based on query type using a lightweight classifier before retrieval
why_interesting: The insight: most teams pick one retrieval strategy and force everything through it. Wrong retrieval produces wrong answers that compound into agent failures. A small LLM classifier in front of the retrieval layer costs less than one bad retrieval. Vector for factual lookup, GraphRAG for multi-hop relational, PageIndex for long structured docs. FinanceBench: vector scores 50%, PageIndex scores 98.7%.

title: Ruflo
description: Agent orchestration platform for Claude — deploy multi-agent workflows with a visual builder and structured output routing
why_interesting: 53k stars. First major orchestration platform built specifically for the Claude ecosystem. The 'single agent framework, many providers' era is giving way to framework-specific orchestration layers. TypeScript, visual workflow builder, supports Claude Code and OpenClaw natively.

title: pentest-ai
description: Offensive security MCP server — wraps 205 pentesting tools and 17 specialist agents behind a single MCP interface
why_interesting: 268 stars, MIT license. The first serious attempt to put offensive security behind MCP. 205 tools (nmap, exploitation, OSINT) accessible to any MCP client. Shows MCP reaching beyond dev tools into security operations. Active commits. Python.

title: Warp Oz Multi-Agent Orchestration
description: Multi-agent orchestration in Warp's Oz — delegate complex tasks across Claude Code, Codex, and Warp Agent with worktree isolation and message passing
why_interesting: 177 likes, 81k views. First terminal-based multi-agent orchestrator that crosses framework boundaries. Each subagent gets its own worktree (local) or Docker container (cloud). The /orchestrate command generates a delegation plan and agents coordinate via structured message passing. This is the 'agent of agents' pattern going mainstream in terminal tools.

title: Plano
description: AI-native proxy and data plane for agentic apps — LLM routing, safety guardrails, orchestration, and observability in one Rust proxy
why_interesting: 6.4k stars, Rust, built on Envoy. The 'Envoy for agents' pattern — sits between your agents and LLM providers handling routing, rate limiting, safety checks, and cost tracking. Most agent teams build this ad-hoc; Plano gives it to you as a drop-in proxy. Solves a real infra gap.

title: Cozeloop
description: Full-lifecycle agent optimization platform — dev, debug, eval, and monitor agents from a single Go service
why_interesting: 5.4k stars, Go, from ByteDance's Coze team. Agent eval + monitoring + prompt management in one platform. The lifecycle angle matters — most tools do eval OR observability, Cozeloop does both plus a playground for iteration. Good fit for teams running agents in production who need to close the feedback loop between monitoring and improvement.

title: CubeSandbox
description: Hardware-isolated sandbox for AI agents built on RustVMM + KVM — boots in under 60ms, uses less than 5MB per instance
why_interesting: From Tencent Cloud. Not containers — actual hardware-level isolation via KVM micro-VMs. E2B SDK compatible. 5.8k stars in 6 weeks, Rust, Apache 2.0. The agent sandbox problem (how do you run untrusted agent code safely?) is one of the unsolved infra gaps. Most solutions use Docker with seccomp. CubeSandbox uses virtualization, which is fundamentally harder to escape. 2000+ concurrent sandboxes on a single node. This is the security layer production agents need.

title: Open Multi-Agent
description: TypeScript-native multi-agent orchestration — turns a goal into a task DAG automatically, with MCP and live tracing, three runtime dependencies
why_interesting: 6.2k stars, MIT, created March 2026. The 3-dependency claim is rare in a space where most frameworks pull in hundreds. Model-agnostic: Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama. The goal-to-DAG pattern means you describe what you want, not how agents coordinate. Built-in live tracing solves the visibility gap. TypeScript-native fills the Node.js ecosystem gap that most agent frameworks ignore.

title: Sandcastle
description: Orchestrate sandboxed coding agents in TypeScript with sandcastle.run() — single API call spins up an isolated agent on Docker, Podman, or Vercel Firecracker microVMs
why_interesting: From Matt Pocock (Total TypeScript). 4.6k stars, MIT, 483 forks. The key insight: agent orchestration needs sandboxing as a first-class concern, not an afterthought. sandcastle.run() handles branch isolation, sandbox provisioning, and merge-back automatically. Provider-agnostic (Docker, Podman, Vercel). This is the 'test runner for agents' pattern — you don't think about the sandbox, you just run. Active commits, 660+ PRs merged.

title: Context Mode — Context Window Optimization for AI Coding Agents (15.5K Stars, HN #1)
description: Context window optimization for AI coding agents — sandboxes tool output, claims 98% reduction in context usage across 15 platforms
why_interesting: 15K stars. #1 on Hacker News with 570+ points. Used at Microsoft, Google, Meta. 98% context reduction. 15 platforms. Not security but massive traction.

title: DeerFlow — ByteDance SuperAgent with Sandboxes, Memory, Skills, Subagents (69K Stars)
description: Open-source long-horizon SuperAgent by ByteDance that researches, codes, and creates. Uses sandboxes, memories, tools, skills, subagents and message gateway to handle tasks from minutes to hours.
why_interesting: 68K+ stars. Handles tasks that take minutes to hours with full agent infrastructure — not a demo wrapper. ByteDance-backed and actively maintained.

title: OpenSandbox — Secure, Fast Sandbox Runtime for AI Agents from Alibaba (10.8K Stars)
description: Secure sandbox runtime for AI agents from Alibaba — extensible plugin architecture for isolation, resource limits, and policy enforcement
why_interesting: 10.7k stars, Apache 2.0, Python. The agent sandbox space is consolidating fast: CubeSandbox (Tencent, KVM micro-VMs), OpenSandbox (Alibaba, plugin-based), microsandbox (local Rust), Sandcastle (Matt Pocock, TypeScript). OpenSandbox's angle is extensibility — plugins for custom isolation policies rather than one-size-fits-all containerization. Active commits. Part of the 'agent runtime isolation' infra layer that production agents require.

title: Microsandbox — Unexploitable Secrets for AI Agents via Hardware-Isolated microVMs (6.2K Stars)
description: Spins up lightweight VMs in milliseconds. Hardware-level isolation. Rootless, embeddable SDK. Key feature: secrets that can't leak — unexploitable secret keys that never enter the VM. Every other sandbox tries to contain what the agent does. This one prevents what the agent can ever know. Written in Rust. Under 100ms boot time.
why_interesting: Contrarian angle: keeps secrets FROM the agent, not just contained. Hardware isolation + unexploitable keys that never enter VM. Rust. 100ms boot. Our exact niche.

title: Memori
description: Agent-native memory infrastructure — LLM-agnostic layer that turns agent execution and conversation into structured, persistent state for production systems
why_interesting: 14.6k stars, Python, 2200 forks. Different from claude-mem (which is session context persistence). Memori is structured state: it captures execution traces, decisions, and conversation turns, then compresses them into retrievable memory that any LLM can query. The agent-memory problem has two layers — short-term context (solved by bigger windows) and long-term structured recall (still unsolved). Memori targets the second. Production systems need agents that remember what happened across sessions without re-reading the full transcript.

title: MassGen
description: Open-source multi-agent scaling system with TUI — agents work in parallel, vote on best solutions via consensus, with checklist-gated quality rounds
why_interesting: 1034 stars. The consensus voting mechanism is genuinely different from other orchestrators. Agents collaborate, vote to converge, and self-evaluate with evolving criteria. Worktree isolation per agent, MCP tool support, checkpoint safety as standalone MCP server. Python/TUI. Fills the "how do multiple agents agree on an answer" gap.

title: Agent Orchestrator
description: Parallel coding agent orchestrator that plans tasks, spawns agents via tmux+git worktrees, and autonomously handles CI fixes, merge conflicts, and code reviews.
why_interesting: Solves the real scaling problem: running multiple coding agents in parallel without them stepping on each other. Uses git worktrees for isolation, tmux for process management. 7K stars, actively maintained.

title: ByteRover CLI
description: Portable memory layer for autonomous coding agents. Formerly Cipher. Works as MCP server providing persistent context across sessions.
why_interesting: Tackles the agent memory gap between sessions without requiring a full RAG pipeline. Portable = works with Claude Code, Codex, any agent. 4.7K stars.

title: cc-sdd (Spec-Driven Development)
description: Turns approved specs into long-running autonomous implementation. Minimal SDD harness with agent skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI.
why_interesting: Interesting approach: instead of letting agents freestyle, constrain them with approved specs first. The spec-as-contract pattern reduces hallucinated implementations.

title: agentmemory
description: Persistent memory for AI coding agents based on real-world benchmarks. Records what your agent does during every session, compresses it with AI, injects the right context back when the next session starts. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Hermes. 4-layer memory architecture: working, episodic, semantic, procedural. 95.2% retrieval accuracy at top-5 on LongMemEval-S.
why_interesting: 15.5K stars in 3 months. Single tweet got 981 bookmarks and 36K views. Agent memory is THE hot topic right now — every coding agent loses context between sessions and this solves it with real benchmarks. Share trigger: 95.2% retrieval accuracy + 4-layer memory model inspired by human cognition.

title: MemOS
description: Self-evolving memory OS for LLM and AI agents. Ultra-persistent memory, hybrid-retrieval (keyword + vector + graph), and cross-task skill reuse. Claims 35.24% token savings through intelligent memory compression and retrieval.
why_interesting: 9.2K stars. The token savings claim (35.24%) is concrete and shareable. Cross-task skill reuse is different from just session memory — it learns across projects. Hybrid retrieval (keyword + vector + graph) is technically interesting vs pure vector approaches.

title: engram
description: Persistent memory system for AI coding agents. Agent-agnostic Go binary with SQLite + FTS5, MCP server, HTTP API, CLI, and TUI. No external dependencies — runs as a single binary.
why_interesting: 3.6K stars. Contrarian approach in a TypeScript-dominated space: pure Go, SQLite-based, no cloud deps. Agent-agnostic means it works with any tool that speaks MCP. Single binary deployment is a real advantage over node-heavy alternatives.

title: osaurus
description: Native macOS harness for AI agents. Any model, persistent memory, autonomous execution, cryptographic identity. Built in Swift. Fully offline. Open source. MCP compatible.
why_interesting: 5.4K stars. Fully offline + crypto identity is a strong contrarian angle in the everything-cloud era. Swift native means it actually uses macOS hardware properly. Share trigger: local-first agent that owns its own identity without any cloud service.

title: ECC
description: Agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond.
why_interesting: 192K stars for agent harness optimization — skills, instincts, memory, security in one system.

title: OpenViking
description: Open-source context database designed specifically for AI Agents. Unifies management of context (memory, resources, skills) through a file system paradigm with hierarchical context delivery and self-evolving.
why_interesting: ByteDance/Volcengine building a context OS for agents. File system paradigm is different from vector-only approaches. 24K stars. Self-evolving context management.

title: memvid
description: Memory layer for AI Agents. Replaces complex RAG pipelines with a serverless, single-file memory layer. Gives agents instant retrieval and long-term memory. Built in Rust.
why_interesting: Replaces entire RAG stacks with a single MP4 file. Rust-based, offline-first, zero infrastructure. 15.5K stars. The "anti-pipeline" approach to agent memory.

title: code-review-graph
description: Local knowledge graph for Claude Code. Builds a persistent map of your codebase so Claude reads only what matters — 6.8x fewer tokens on reviews and up to 49x on daily coding tasks. 19+ languages. Runs fully local. No API keys.
why_interesting: Reduces Claude Code tool calls by 94% by indexing codebase into a knowledge graph upfront instead of scanning files. 17K stars in ~3 months. Viral on Twitter (264+ likes). The "stop scanning, start querying" approach to agent code intelligence.

title: Mirage
description: A unified virtual filesystem for AI agents. Gives every agent a consistent file interface regardless of backend. Works with Claude Code, LangChain, OpenAI agents. TypeScript + Python.
why_interesting: Only 15 days old, already 2.5K stars. Solves the "every agent has a different IO model" problem. VFS abstraction means agents can read/write without caring about where data lives. Fresh project with strong traction.

title: smallcode
description: AI coding agent optimized for small LLMs. Hits 87% benchmark score with only a 4B-active parameter model. Proves you dont need massive models for real coding tasks.
why_interesting: Hot take material: 4B model beating agents that run on 70B+ models. 979 stars in 3 days. Directly challenges the "you need the biggest model" narrative. Cost implications are huge — run a coding agent on a potato.

title: ARGO
description: Open-source local AI agent platform. Manus-style autonomous task execution running 100% on your laptop. No cloud, no subscription. Multi-agent task engine with planning, reflection, tool chaining. Ollama + HuggingFace + OpenAI/Claude/DeepSeek. Full MCP support. Local RAG.
why_interesting: Directly challenges $39/month Manus. No cloud dependency, no data leaving your machine. The "Manus but local" positioning is viral. Human-in-the-loop planning step. Native apps for Mac/Windows/Linux.

title: mcp2cli
description: Turn any MCP, OpenAPI, or GraphQL server into a CLI — at runtime, with zero codegen. Every MCP server loads ALL tool definitions on EVERY turn. mcp2cli converts them to simple commands the agent calls only when needed. Saves thousands of tokens per turn.
why_interesting: Practical cost-saver for anyone running agents with MCP. The insight that MCP burns tokens on unused tool definitions is a real problem. 2.1K stars. Zero codegen at runtime is clever engineering.

title: Dulus
description: Free CLI agent that harvests Gemini (guest, no login), Claude.ai, Kimi, Qwen, DeepSeek browser sessions and turns them into tool-calling agents. Reads and edits files, runs Bash, greps repos, browses the web, ships commits. All from terminal at $0.
why_interesting: Provocative approach — instead of paying for API access, it piggybacks on free browser sessions. 625 stars. The "why pay for APIs" angle is contrarian enough to get attention. Practical for devs who want agent capabilities without API bills.

title: Zerolang
description: Agent-first programming language by Vercel Labs. Small regular syntax agents learn on the fly. Structured diagnostics, deterministic tooling, deep stdlib. Written in C, Apache-2.0.
why_interesting: 4.1K stars in 6 days. Top tweet got 58K views. First language designed specifically for agents as primary users. Compare: prompts vs agent-native code.

title: Photo-agents
description: Autonomous self-evolving agents with vision-grounded layered memory. Perceive/reason/act loop. Agents write own skills from real success. Multi-provider LLM router, browser automation, sandboxed code exec. Python.
why_interesting: Self-evolving agent narrative exploding (dair_ai survey 252K views). Vision+memory+self-written-skills combo is unique. 1K stars in 2 weeks.

title: OpenSquilla
description: Token-efficient microkernel AI agent. Local model router sends each turn to cheapest capable model. Persistent memory, layered sandbox, web search, on-device embeddings. 20+ LLM providers. Python.
why_interesting: Directly addresses rising API costs (GPT-5.5 2x, Claude +46%). Model routing = pay less for same results. 1.3K stars, Apache-2.0.

title: OctoTools
description: Agentic framework with extensible tool cards for complex reasoning. Planner+executor loop, standardized tool metadata. Broad LLM support. Python, MIT.
why_interesting: Tool-card pattern is interesting for modular agent design. 1.4K stars. Older (Feb 2025). Lower urgency.

title: EverOS
description: Build, evaluate, and integrate long-term memory for self-evolving agents. Python, Apache-2.0.
why_interesting: Combines memory layer WITH eval framework. 5.4K stars. Most agent memory repos just store. This one evaluates whether the memory actually helps. Also has self-evolving agent architecture built in.

title: SimpleMem
description: Efficient lifelong memory for LLM agents — text and multimodal. Python, MIT.
why_interesting: Research-backed memory system that handles text AND multimodal. 3.3K stars. Most memory tools are text-only. This one extends to images and structured data. MIT license makes it easy to adopt.

title: moltis
description: Secure persistent personal agent server in Rust. One binary, sandboxed execution, multi-provider LLMs, voice, memory, messaging integrations. Runs on your hardware.
why_interesting: Rust binary with sandboxed execution. Single deployable unit. Connects to Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, Teams. 2.7K stars and growing. The "run on your hardware" angle is the story — no cloud dependency, no vendor lock-in.

title: oh-my-claudecode
description: Teams-first multi-agent orchestration for Claude Code. Parallel execution, agent specialization.
why_interesting: 34K stars. The "teams-first" approach is the differentiator — not just multi-agent, but structured team roles with parallel execution. This is the direction agent frameworks are converging toward.

title: TradingAgents
description: Multi-agent LLM financial trading framework. Research Desk, Quant Team, Trading Floor, and Risk Management as separate agents orchestrated together. Python.
why_interesting: 78K stars. Multi-agent architecture applied to financial trading — each role (researcher, quant, trader, risk) is a separate LLM agent. Practical example of multi-agent coordination solving a complex domain problem. The bull/bear debate mechanism between agents is novel.

title: zeroclaw
description: Fast, small, fully autonomous AI personal assistant infrastructure. Rust-based. Deploy anywhere, any OS, any platform. Modular swap-anything architecture.
why_interesting: 31K stars, created Feb 2026 (3 months old). Rust means real sandboxing, not theater. "Deploy anywhere" claim backed by cross-platform binary. The "swap anything" modular design is the interesting architecture choice — lets you swap LLM providers, memory backends, tool integrations independently.

title: MCP Toolbox for Databases
description: Open-source MCP server by Google for databases. Supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, BigQuery, Spanner, MongoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, ClickHouse, CockroachDB, Oracle, TiDB, Firestore, and more. Go.
why_interesting: 15K stars. Google official. 20+ database backends via single MCP server. This is the "just works" layer between agents and data — no more custom database connectors per agent. Go means single binary deployment.

title: omo (oh-my-openagent)
description: The best agent harness. Previously oh-my-opencode. 58.8K stars. Supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode. Modular skills, orchestration, agent loop — all in one harness.
why_interesting: 58.8K stars in 6 months. Started as oh-my-opencode, evolved into a universal agent harness. The author also built lightweight agent loop that uses <40% CPU and 3GB RAM vs bloated alternatives. Claude Code + Codex + Cursor all supported.

title: agent-lightning
description: Microsoft open-source RL trainer for AI agents. Works with LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI SDK, or plain Python. Captures prompts, tool calls, rewards as structured events. Trains improved prompts or policy weights automatically.
why_interesting: 17.2K stars. Microsoft built an RL loop that makes ANY agent framework better without rewriting prompts. Agnostic to your stack — drop in agl.emit(), pick algorithm, agent improves. First time RL for agent optimization is this accessible.

title: html-anything
description: Agentic HTML editor — your local AI agent writes the HTML, you ship it. 75 skills × 9 surfaces (magazine, deck, poster, XHS/tweet, prototype, data report, Hyperframes). Sandboxed preview, 1-click publish to WeChat/X/Zhihu. Zero API key required.
why_interesting: 4.4K stars in 3 weeks. 75 skills, 9 output surfaces, zero API keys. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode. The skill-based architecture is clean — composable agent primitives, not monolithic templates.

title: AiSOC
description: Open-source AI-powered Security Operations Center. Alert fusion, purple-team drills, agent-assisted triage, MITRE ATT&CK investigation. MIT-licensed, self-hostable. Python + Next.js.
why_interesting: 1.1K stars. First real open-source AI SOC. Agent-assisted alert triage with MITRE ATT&CK mapping. The agent architecture is interesting — separate agents for detection, investigation, and response. Self-hostable, MIT license.

title: holaOS
description: Agent OS that turns repeat work into running AI work-streams. Electron-based, MCP-compatible, with persistent memory and proactive AI runtime. TypeScript.
why_interesting: 5.6K stars in 2 months. Agent OS category is heating up — not just a harness but a workspace that learns your patterns.

title: Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit — Runtime Policy Enforcement for Every Agent Tool Call (1.9K Stars)
description: Microsoft toolkit that intercepts every tool call, resource access, and inter-agent message BEFORE execution. Deterministic, sub-millisecond, auditable. Covers 10/10 OWASP Agentic Top 10. PyPI, npm, NuGet.
why_interesting: Microsoft shipping agent security tooling that covers ALL OWASP agentic top-10. Signal that agent governance is becoming enterprise requirement.

title: TEN Framework
description: Open-source framework for conversational voice AI agents. Multi-modal, real-time voice + video. Python.
why_interesting: 10.6K stars. Voice agents are the next frontier after text agents — TEN is the leading framework in this niche.

title: nexent
description: Zero-code platform for auto-generating production-grade AI agents using Harness Engineering principles. Unified tools, skills, memory, orchestration with constraints, feedback loops, control planes. Python, MIT.
why_interesting: 4.6K stars. Harness engineering applied to agents — the no-code angle could be interesting for non-dev audience.

title: boxlite
description: Compute substrate for AI agents: lightweight on laptop, elastic to cloud. Rust + TypeScript, Apache 2.0. Embedded, self-hosted, serverless.
why_interesting: Laptop-to-cloud agent sandbox. Same space as microsandbox but cloud-elastic. Good comparativo angle.

title: mcpc
description: Universal CLI client for MCP by Apify. Persistent sessions, stdio/HTTP, OAuth 2.1, tasks, JSON output, proxy for AI sandboxes, x402 support.
why_interesting: MCP ecosystem maturing — a universal CLI client means MCP is becoming infrastructure, not just a protocol.

title: agent-safehouse
description: Sandbox your local AI agents so they can read/write only what they need. Shell-based, minimal.
why_interesting: Minimal approach to agent sandboxing — opposite end of spectrum from heavy frameworks. Good for "just works" angle.

title: Hive (aden-hive)
description: Multi-Agent Harness for Production AI. Python framework with self-improving agents, human-in-the-loop, agent skills, supports OpenAI and Anthropic.
why_interesting: 10.4K stars, production-grade multi-agent harness. Self-improving agents + human-in-the-loop. Topic aligned with hot Anthropic agents discussion (130K+ views on Twitter). Strong viral potential: production agents framework with real architecture.

title: Motus (lithos-ai)
description: Open-source agent-serving project. From the team behind Motus Tracing (356 likes, 27K views on Twitter). Agent observability infrastructure.
why_interesting: Agent observability is consolidating as a theme (per persona_memory). This is the serving/infra companion to Motus Tracing which got massive engagement. 455 stars and growing. Fits our "agent sandboxing/infra consolidating" pattern.

title: evilsocket/audit — 8-Stage Vulnerability-Discovery Agent (Cloudflare Glasswing Pipeline)
description: From the creator of bettercap. Reimplementation of Cloudflare Project Glasswing: 8 narrow agents with deliberate disagreement and reachability gates beat one big model at finding bugs. MIT licensed, no API key needed with claude login. Stages: Recon → Hunt → Verify → Reach → Disprove → Feedback → Triage → Report.
why_interesting: Contrarian angle: one big model can't find bugs. 8 narrow agents that disagree with each other can. From bettercap creator. Based on Cloudflare's published research. First agent that goes from recon to verified, reachable CVE.

title: Agent Executor (AX)
description: Google open source distributed agent runtime. General purpose runtime for dynamic scheduling, resumption, auto recovery, auditing, and trajectory branching from kernel snapshots in agentic workloads. Written in Go. Announced at Google I/O 2026 by @rakyll.
why_interesting: Google-backed agent runtime addressing the unsolved infra problem of productionizing long-running agentic workloads. Scheduling, resumption, and trajectory branching from kernel snapshots. 25K+ views on announcement tweet. Directly competes with the scheduling/gap that most agent frameworks hand-wave.

title: IronClaw — Agent OS Focused on Privacy, Security and Extensibility (12.3K Stars)
description: Agent OS focused on privacy, security and extensibility. Written in Rust with WASM sandboxing and encrypted credential vault where the LLM never sees your API keys.
why_interesting: 12K stars. Rust-based agent runtime with WASM sandboxing is exactly the wire-level enforcement angle that resonated with infra builders (proven by Ryan Dahl engagement). Encrypted credential vault solves the real problem of agents needing API access without leaking secrets.

title: AI-Infra-Guard — Full-Stack AI Red Teaming Platform by Tencent (3.8K Stars)
description: A full-stack AI Red Teaming platform securing AI ecosystems via OpenClaw Security Scan, Agent Scan, Skills Scan, MCP scan, AI Infra scan and LLM jailbreak evaluation.
why_interesting: Tencent-backed open-source AI red teaming platform that covers the full attack surface: agents, MCP servers, skills, prompts, and infrastructure. 3.7K stars. Pushed today. Agent security is our highest-engagement topic — Ryan Dahl thread proved network-layer security resonates with infra builders.

title: supply-chain-guard (pc-style)
description: Local supply-chain install gate for npm packages and VS Code extensions with Socket, Codex integration.
why_interesting: Every AI coding agent runs npm install with zero human review. This gates installs at the local level with Socket + Codex checks. Created today. Chen Avnery tweet about autonomous amplifiers got 148 views — supply chain for agents is a live topic.

title: Studio (decocms)
description: Open-source control plane for your AI agents. Connect tools, hire agents, track every token and dollar.
why_interesting: First open-source agent control plane with cost tracking. 373 stars. One bad agent loop = five-figure model bill, and most teams have zero visibility. Pushed today. Practical value for anyone running agents in production.

title: claude-in-box (jiangmuran)
description: Portable Claude Code dev environment in a Docker container. Multi-session, hook-driven, with persistent workspace.
why_interesting: Dockerized Claude Code with multi-session support and hooks. Created today. Solves the real problem of reproducible coding agent environments. Go-based. 24 stars but very fresh and practical.

title: CVE-2026-46354 — Coder Agent Token Theft via Azure Signature Bypass (CVSS 9.1)

description: DeepSeek made their 75% V4-Pro price cut permanent. Model runs at 1/35th the cost of Claude Opus 4.7/GPT-5.5. Also found: per-model tool input repair tables (avg 4 per model), capability flag negotiation per upstream, and thinking-mode regressions from wrong provider defaults.
why_interesting: The 'open models are bad at coding' narrative is usually a harness problem, not a model problem. One HTTP header (cache pinning) gave 6-8x TTFT improvement. The approve button shows one path but symlink resolution writes to another — agents rewrite their own MCP server configs with full user privileges. Zero-click trigger in CI environments. why_interesting: The core assumption behind agent safety (human reviews every action) is theater if the filesystem lies to you. This breaks ALL major coding agents simultaneously. The approval prompt path ≠ actual write path when symlinks are involved. Agent rewrites its own MCP config with user privileges. Zero-click in CI. This is an architecture flaw, not a vendor bug.
